Fantastic, I feel dumb for not googling it to begin with, but thanks! From the youtubing I did it looks a lot easier than a car, easy peasy. Thank you for your time, I appreciate it.

DOT3 and DOT4 shouldn't hurt your car after mixing, as both are glycol based, but you can't be sure certain about their performance after mixing. If I were you, I'd simply bleed out all DOT3/4 and pour DOT4, especially if it's very old.

If I were you, I would just make sure it's not DOT5, as it's impossible to mix DOT4 and DOT5. DOT5 is silicon based, and if they are mixed together they can be unpredictable or straight harmful for your installation. Therefore before changing between DOT4 and DOT5, all remains of the old fluid should be thoroughly cleaned. Fortunately there's also DOT5.1 which has properties similar to DOT5 but is also based on glycol, so it can be safely used after bleeding out all DOT4.

I know you know that, but after this change it'd be good to test the breaks in a safe location before use, anyway.
